slide.title: change-saga theme: init, check, preview
slide.takeaway: init writes a commented starter, check validates and measures WCAG AA contrast in both modes with an exit code for CI, and preview opens light and dark side by side.

item.label: theme init writes a starter
item.description: Every token with its light and dark defaults, grouped and commented out; it names the file it wrote and refuses to replace a theme without --force.

item.label: theme check validates, then measures
item.description: Invalid exits 1 naming each line; valid measures contrast and exits 3 naming each failing pair; without a theme it checks the defaults.

item.label: The key pairs, in both modes
item.description: WCAG relative luminance on the resolved values of each scheme; a translucent colour is composited over what it sits on.

item.label: theme preview opens /theme
item.description: A page of its own: swatches, chrome samples, and a generated diagram, each pane scoped to one scheme, with problems and contrast failures listed above.

item.label: Help, grammar, and skill
item.description: The theme family is dispatched like diagram, listed in help, declared in the grammar that spec publishes, and taught by a skill reference.

item.label: preview reuses any running reviewer
item.description: It does not replace a comparison reviewer with an observing one.
item.body: You might expect preview to start its own server; it opens /theme on the Saga's running background reviewer whatever its opening, since the theme does not depend on it, and starts one only when none is running.

item.label: CLI and end-to-end tests
item.description: init and --force, check's exit codes and named pairs, validate's lines, and Playwright recolouring the reviewer and a slide by OS preference and by toggle.
